description: Espionage was a common tool of statecraft in classical civilizations, used to gather intelligence on enemy armies, political rivals, fortifications, and alliances. Greeks, Persians, Carthaginians, Romans, and others employed scouts, informants, defectors, merchants, diplomats, and covert agents. Spies could reveal troop movements, spread misinformation, bribe officials, or uncover plots, making intelligence an important complement to diplomacy and warfare.
